title: Eight Is Great
lede: A bank set a target of eight products per household. The metric counted every account its staff opened, including the ones customers never asked for. When a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring.

commit.title: YOUR GUESS
commit.prompt: Of every 1,000 accounts opened, how many did customers never authorise?

chapters.eyebrow: ONE MARK = 165,000 ACCOUNTS · JAN 2009 TO SEP 2016
chapters.title: A thousand accounts

captions: Target: 8 products per customer. Your team is hitting it.
One bank ran on that exact target. Your guess first.
Of 1,000 accounts opened, how many were never authorised?
Feb 2015: 6.13 on average. One household in four had 8+.
2016: 2.1 M accounts flagged. 5,300 fired. $185 M fines.
2017: the full review says 3.5 M. 2020: $3 B to settle.
165 M accounts opened, 2009 to 2016. Here are 1,000.
The metric counted every one as a product sold.
The review flagged 21. The metric still counted them.
Your guess, outlined. The review found 21.
21 is the floor. Unused products sold were counted too.
Monday: what could move this number with nothing behind it?
Limits: 3.5 M is an estimate. One bank, one metric.

brand.takeaway: When a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring.

sources: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Consent Order, In the Matter of Wells Fargo Bank, N.A., File No. 2016-CFPB-0015, 8 September 2016, and press release of the same day ($100 M penalty; OCC $35 M; Los Angeles $50 M).
Independent Directors of the Board of Wells Fargo & Company, Sales Practices Investigation Report, 10 April 2017 (Shearman & Sterling LLP).
Wells Fargo & Company, "Wells Fargo Reports Completion of Expanded Third-Party Review of Retail Banking Accounts", press release, 31 August 2017 (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1).

U.S. Department of Justice, "Wells Fargo Agrees to Pay $3 Billion to Resolve Criminal and Civil Investigations into Sales Practices Involving the Opening of Millions of Accounts without Customer Authorization", 21 February 2020, with the Deferred Prosecution Agreement, Exhibit A, Statement of Facts.
Wells Fargo & Company, Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2015 (retail banking household cross-sell 6.13 in February 2015; goal of eight; one in four households with eight or more).

M. Strathern, "'Improving ratings': audit in the British University system", European Review 5(3), 1997, 305-321; after C. A. E. Goodhart, "Problems of Monetary Management: The U.K. Experience", Reserve Bank of Australia, 1975.
honest: The 3.5 million is the bank's own review estimate of potentially unauthorised accounts: it may include some accounts customers did authorise, and it does not count unwanted products sold with consent, which the metric also counted.
The grid is a constructed teaching object: 165 million accounts drawn as 1,000 marks, 21 of them red (3.53 M ÷ 165 M). The positions of the red marks are a seeded shuffle, not data.
One bank and one metric. Goodhart's law is a tendency, not a proof that every target goes bad.
